items.title: arXiv imposes rate limit on paper submissions to stem the AI slop tide
items.summary: arXiv, the preprint paper repository, is seeing so many low-quality submissions, with AI tools helping drive the surge, that it has imposed a hard limit of two new submissions per month per submitter, regardless of whether they were produced solely by humans or with help from AI tools. After becoming an independent nonprofit over the summer following 25 years under Cornell University’s stewardship, arXiv continued to rely on a “practical limit” in place that gave moderators the ability to determine whether someone was submitting too many papers. Like everything good and pure in this world, AI has ruined that, too, necessitating some strict new limits. “arXiv now limits submitters to up to two submissions per calendar month, with a limit of three total active submissions at any given time,” arXiv community engagement manager Kat Boboris wrote in a Thursday announcement of the change, which was effective immediately. According to an arXiv spokesperson, an active paper is one that has been submitted, is under consideration and review, but not yet published on the site.

items.title: Apple changes full-disk access permissions to curb abuse from AI agents
items.summary: Apple says it is changing its macOS privacy settings to stop third-party app developers from misusing them to access message histories. Friday’s announcement comes two weeks after tech columnist Jason Aten said that Meta’s new general-purpose AI agent Muse sent him an unsolicited notification referencing a thread between him and a co-worker over Apple Messages. Aten said he never granted Muse permissions to read his messages and had assumed they were off-limits. Social media last week blew up with masses of people who agreed and said the incident showed that AI assistants given access to calendars, emails, messages, shopping accounts, and other resources are akin to a skill saw or other power tool. While potentially useful, they can do real damage if not used carefully.

items.title: ShinyHunters hacker reportedly detained in Jordan, aiding FBI
items.summary: A suspected ShinyHunters hacking group member known online as "Rey" has reportedly been detained in Jordan and is cooperating with the FBI to help locate other members of the extortion group. According to Reuters, Jordanian authorities detained Rey, identified as Saif al-Din Khader, this week, with two sources saying he was taken into custody on Tuesday. Two sources familiar with the arrest told Reuters that Khader is now helping the FBI and international law enforcement agencies locate other group members. One source said Khader is walking law enforcement through his electronic devices and digital communications to help identify and locate his alleged co-conspirators.

items.title: MI5 Says China’s MSS Funded Research Involving 100+ U.K.-Linked Academics
items.summary: The U.K.'s domestic intelligence and security agency has warned that more than 100 academics have helped China boost its intelligence gathering efforts on behalf of Beijing's state security service. In a "Security Service Espionage Alert" issued on September 30, 2026, MI5 said the "primary purpose of the China General Technology Research Institute (CGTRI) 中国通用技术研究院 is to fund research that directly improves Chinese Ministry of State Security (MSS) technical capability for espionage." CGTRI, also known as the China Academy of General Technology (CAGT), is assessed to be a front company for MSS. The body, per MI5, funds academic research in China on topics including artificial intelligence (AI), cybersecurity, covert communications systems, and steganography.
